title: Design and generate an Aria-to-VCF management migration architecture
prompt:
Create the implementation architecture for moving the management estate in `estate/inventory.json` to the target VMware Cloud Foundation release. This is an architecture deliverable, not a prose migration explainer.

Before implementing it, use genuine network research to read current Broadcom-published material covering the supported transitions from each inventoried vRealize/Aria product, content and configuration compatibility, end-of-general-support boundaries, and the NSX Edge sizing/uplink guidance relevant to the stated throughput. Record what you actually consulted in `research/consulted-sources.md` as a Markdown table with the columns `Title`, `URL`, `Access date`, and `Decision informed`, using one row per source and `YYYY-MM-DD` access dates. Every URL must be real and reachable. Choose the sources yourself; do not treat the local compatibility snapshot as a substitute for live research. If current material differs from the frozen snapshot, record the difference, but build the artifact to the snapshot because it is the installed design authority for this exercise.

Implement a PowerShell module at `VcfAriaMigration/VcfAriaMigration.psd1` and `.psm1`. It must export only `New-VcfAriaMigrationPlan`, whose parameters are `-InventoryPath`, `-CompatibilityPath`, `-InstallerSpecificationPath`, and `-OutputPath`. The environment provides `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` 13.5.0.25380678. Declare it as a required module, use its genuine SDDC Manager operation discovery during generation, and do not vendor or replace any VMware SDK module. The function must read the three supplied inputs, derive the design rather than embed an already-rendered plan, and write deterministic UTF-8 JSON to `-OutputPath`.

The checked-in result is `architecture/migration-plan.json`. It must validate against the JSON Schema embedded in `spec/installer-spec.json` and follow `spec/compatibility-snapshot.json`. Include the ordered transition of every source product and exact version to its target component; enumerate each inventoried content/configuration item that carries forward and how, each item that is abandoned and why, and the gates for every step. Include lifecycle boundaries. Place and size VCF Operations, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations for Logs in the supplied VCF inventory. Derive the NSX Edge form factor and dual-fabric uplink/vNIC layout from the failure-survivable throughput requirement, including capacity, VLAN, MTU, BGP, and placement details.

Do not modify `estate/`, `spec/`, or `.protected/`. Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py` from the repository root; it validates the artifact schema before any semantic checks and then regenerates the artifact through your module.
